provenance.note: `Config` takes a whole `SignifyClient`, as `KeyEvents` and `KeyStates` do, so the real client is driven with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a recorder that signs its answers as a KERIA agent would. The clock and the agent's key are pinned. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode is the one `coring.test.ts` publishes and has never protected anything.

notes.path: the path is a template literal with nothing interpolated into it, so this is the only endpoint in the port whose address carries no caller input at all
notes.body: the reference passes `null` as the request data and `SignifyClient.fetch` sends `null` for a GET regardless, so no body is written either way
notes.response: `AgentConfig` declares exactly one optional field, `iurls`, and the reference returns `res.json()` with no validation — so any JSON at all is accepted and typed as an `AgentConfig` at compile time only

calls.name: config_with_introductions
calls.note: the ordinary answer: a list of introduction OOBIs

calls.name: config_empty_list
calls.note: an agent configured with no introductions at all

calls.name: config_absent_field
calls.note: an answer omitting the field entirely, which the schema permits and which is not the same as an empty list

calls.name: config_unknown_fields
calls.note: an answer carrying fields the schema does not declare, which the reference keeps and this port ignores

calls.name: config_wrong_shape
calls.note: an answer whose `iurls` is not a list of strings — the reference types this `AgentConfig` at compile time and returns it unchecked

pinned_confirmations.note: the one path `coring.test.ts` asserts is produced here by the reference's own class, and every one of the five answers produces the same request — the address carries no caller input at all

the_answer_is_never_validated.note: `get` returns `res.json()` cast to `AgentConfig`, so an answer whose `iurls` is a string — or is not an object at all — is handed to the caller as though it were configuration. The type exists only at compile time.
the_answer_is_never_validated.rust_decision: decoded: an answer that is not an `AgentConfig` is `ClientError::Api` rather than a value a caller will misread. The wrong-shaped answer recorded here is proven refused.

unknown_fields_are_kept.note: `res.json()` returns whatever the agent sent, so undeclared fields survive into the value a caller holds
unknown_fields_are_kept.rust_decision: ignored, which is the shared API types' rule for a schema without an index signature: `AgentConfig` declares one field and captures nothing else. A caller who needs an undeclared field is reading a schema this port does not have.

an_absent_list_is_not_an_empty_one.note: the schema marks `iurls` optional, so an agent may omit it; the reference hands back `undefined` in one case and `[]` in the other, and nothing in its own code tells them apart
an_absent_list_is_not_an_empty_one.rust_decision: reproduced as `Option<Vec<String>>`, so the two stay distinguishable — an agent that has not been configured is not an agent configured with nothing

the_path_carries_no_input.note: the path is a template literal with nothing interpolated, which makes this the only endpoint in the port with no dynamic component — and so the only one where the reference's unencoded interpolation cannot bite
the_path_carries_no_input.rust_decision: reproduced exactly; there is nothing to encode and nothing to validate
